claims.text: The modeled FeNiCrCoCu coating is 21 Å thick and is adhered to a single-crystal Cu substrate.
The coating and Cu substrate initially have FCC structures with [100], [010], and [001] orientations.
The virtual indenter is driven at 10 m/s to a depth of 30 Å over 300 ps and unloaded at the same speed over 300 ps.
The simulations compare temperatures of 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K.
The coating's overall wear resistance remains relatively stable from 300 K through 600 K.
A modest reduction in dislocation density up to 600 K slightly increases the elastic modulus.
The slight increase in elastic modulus caused by reduced dislocation density maintains wear resistance up to 600 K.
Above approximately 900 K, the lattice rapidly becomes disordered.
Above approximately 900 K, dislocation density decreases and the HCP atom fraction increases.
Rapid lattice disorder and increased HCP atom fraction above 900 K cause lattice softening.
Lattice softening above 900 K decreases hardness and elastic modulus.
Above 900 K, the dominant deformation response shifts from stacking faults to lattice disorder.
The high-temperature structural and deformation changes cause a sharp decrease in wear resistance above 900 K.
Tangential force and friction coefficient increase with temperature.
Friction coefficient and tangential force exhibit significant fluctuations above 900 K relative to 300 K.
At 300 K, the lattice is ordered, dislocation density is higher, and wear resistance is optimal.
The critical temperature for the sharp deterioration in wear performance is around 900 K.

contradictions.description: The stated measurement list omits wear resistance, hardness, and tangential force, even though the falsification rule depends directly on those outcomes. Friction coefficient alone is not established as a direct measurement of wear resistance or hardness.
